text: Patent application filing fees in India under Patents Rules 2003 First Schedule: For natural persons, the fee is Rs 1,600 for e-filing and Rs 1,750 for physical filing. For startups, small entities, and educational institutions, the fee is Rs 4,000 for e-filing and Rs 4,400 for physical filing. For other applicants (large entities/corporations), the fee is Rs 8,000 for e-filing and Rs 8,800 for physical filing. These fees apply to applications with up to 10 claims and up to 30 pages of specification.

Additional fees for claims beyond 10 in a patent application: For each claim in excess of 10, natural persons pay Rs 320 per claim (e-filing) or Rs 350 (physical). Startups and small entities pay Rs 800 per claim (e-filing) or Rs 880 (physical). Other applicants pay Rs 1,600 per claim (e-filing) or Rs 1,750 (physical). These fees are cumulative and added to the base filing fee.

Additional fees for specification pages beyond 30 in a patent application: For each page in excess of 30, natural persons pay Rs 160 per page (e-filing) or Rs 175 (physical). Startups and small entities pay Rs 400 per page (e-filing) or Rs 440 (physical). Other applicants pay Rs 800 per page (e-filing) or Rs 880 (physical).

Request for Examination (RFE) fee under Patents Rules 2003: Natural persons pay Rs 4,000 (e-filing) or Rs 4,400 (physical). Startups and small entities pay Rs 10,000 (e-filing) or Rs 11,000 (physical). Other applicants pay Rs 20,000 (e-filing) or Rs 22,000 (physical). RFE must be filed within 48 months from the priority date or filing date, whichever is earlier.

Early publication request fee for patent applications: Natural persons pay Rs 2,500 (e-filing) or Rs 2,750 (physical). Startups and small entities pay Rs 6,250 (e-filing) or Rs 6,875 (physical). Other applicants pay Rs 12,500 (e-filing) or Rs 13,750 (physical). Early publication expedites the publication of the application before the standard 18-month period.

Patent renewal fees in India must be paid annually starting from the 3rd year after the date of patent. Fees increase progressively: Years 3-6 are lower, Years 7-10 are moderate, Years 11-15 are higher, and Years 16-20 are highest. For natural persons, Year 3-6 renewal is Rs 800/year, Year 7-10 is Rs 2,400/year, Year 11-15 is Rs 4,800/year, and Year 16-20 is Rs 8,000/year. Failure to pay renewal fees results in patent lapse.

For reduced patent fees, a 'startup' under Indian patent rules must be registered with DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) and meet the Startup India criteria: annual turnover not exceeding Rs 100 crore, entity age not more than 10 years from incorporation, and working towards innovation or improvement of products/services. Proof of DPIIT recognition is required when filing.

A 'small entity' for reduced patent fees includes enterprises registered under MSME Act with investment in plant/machinery up to Rs 10 crore and turnover up to Rs 50 crore. Evidence of MSME/Udyam registration must be provided. Educational institutions recognized by law also qualify for small entity fees.
